feature.summary: AGI Mobile stores chats in an encrypted SQLite database whose 256-bit key sits in device secure storage, and can run a small model on the phone for free without an account. Onboarding checks the device and recommends a model. The Electron desktop does not run on-device models; only the retained Tauri code checks a local model server.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps mobile data encrypted on the device and runs inference there when the phone supports it. (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts:19-30,130-160; packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts)
purpose.why_it_exists: Local mode must work without an account, keep work on the device and make no hidden cloud calls. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 7.1)
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile users who want private, free, offline chat.
problems_solved: Readable chats if the phone is lost (encryption).
Needing an account or payment for basic chat.
Not knowing whether a device can run a model.
use_cases: Chat on a plane with no network.
Finish onboarding and download a recommended model.
Check tokens per second in Performance settings.

where_to_find_it: Mobile onboarding screen 'Set up local chat on <device name>.' (onboarding.tsx:~700).
Mobile Settings, Performance: 'Device Tier', 'Benchmark This Device', 'Show performance chip in chat' (performance.tsx:594,940,1077).
Desktop Tauri build (retained internal): local model server health monitor (App.tsx:746-752).
prerequisites: A supported phone; downloading a model needs storage and network; Local use needs no sign-in (doc: docs/product/requirements.md M-US-001).
screens_and_controls: 'Recommended' badge, 'Pick a different model', 'Continue without downloading', 'Sign in to use Cloud', 'Continue' and 'Skip for now' (onboarding.tsx:648-810).
When unsupported: '<model> is unavailable on this device.', 'Browse local models', 'Continue without a local model' (onboarding.tsx:684-686,777-794).
Download screen: 'The download continues if you leave this screen.', 'Try again', 'Continue to chat' (onboarding.tsx:880-916).
journey: Open the app for the first time.
Screen shows a recommended model with download size.
Download over wifi or confirm cellular.
Start chatting; chats are saved to the encrypted database.
feedback_and_outputs: Download progress, speed and error with retry (onboarding.tsx:880-905).
Local data reset notice if the database could not be read (localDataReset.ts; LocalDataResetNotice test).
settings: Performance chip toggle; model picker; installed models store (installedModels.ts).

working: Encrypted SQLite through expo-sqlite with SQLCipher enabled (app.config.js:454); key is 32 random bytes in hex kept in secure storage, this-device-only, id agi_sqlcipher_db_key_v1 (db.ts:23-60).
Schema migrations on open using PRAGMA user_version (db.ts:105-122).

An unreadable database (for example restored on another phone without its key) is renamed aside, not deleted, and the person is told (db.ts:76-95); removal of set-aside copies happens only inside the data export and delete flow (services/dsarExport.ts:432-452).

Three-tier local runtime selection: system model, ExecuTorch-based, and GGUF-based; capability detection by platform and RAM (packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts; capabilities.ts:1-60; tier3.ts:1-60).
Multimodal local models need enough RAM and verified artifacts (multimodal.ts exports in index.ts).
Onboarding decides the tier and recommended model (onboarding.tsx:158-215).
incomplete: Chrome, VS Code and CLI use of this on-device package: not read.
disconnected_or_disabled: Electron desktop refuses local inference commands (dispatcher.ts:3234-3244).
Tauri desktop health monitor runs only when isTauri (App.tsx:746-752) and checks a local model server (ollamaHealthService.ts:1-50), a different mechanism from the on-device package.
not_available: Web: no local database or on-device model found.

established.statement: S104.11: a client keeps data in an encrypted local database on the device.
S104.26: the area item about on-device models; mobile loads the on-device runtime at runtime.
Local mode: no AGI account required, local storage by default, no hidden provider call, fails closed.
The user is not forced to sign in for Local; first chat does not call BYOK or Cloud routes; no-model state has setup guidance.
Mobile v1 is small on-device Local models plus signed-in Managed Free; no mobile BYOK in v1.

acceptance_criteria: First launch without an account reaches a chat with a local model or clear guidance.
Chats persist after restart and the database file is not readable as plain SQLite.
Restoring a backup on a new phone shows the reset notice and keeps the old file aside.
An unsupported device shows '<model> is unavailable on this device.' with browse and continue options.
Local chat makes no network call to Cloud or BYOK routes.
Performance screen shows device tier and benchmark.
inferred: Local inference is free of any subscription because the code path has no entitlement check (not found in local-llm files read) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Resolve the desktop conflict: the product says on-device inference on desktop is free, while the public desktop refuses it; record an owner decision.
[proposed] Add a visible label of what happens to the set-aside database.

steps.what_happens: App opens the database: reads or creates the key from secure storage, opens, applies PRAGMA key, WAL, migrations.
Onboarding reads device capabilities and picks a model.
Model files download from the model host.
Local chat sends messages to the on-device runtime and streams tokens back.
Messages are written to the encrypted database.

Lost on device change; database then set aside (db.ts:76-95)
Managed by installedModels and picker; delete path unknown

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Local models come from the local catalog in the local-llm package and are chosen by role and device tier; no provider key or Cloud call is used for them. Which exact models are offered is catalog data, not named here.

access_and_usage.account: Not required for Local (doc: requirements.md M-US-001). Cloud route in onboarding needs sign-in.
access_and_usage.permissions: Storage for models; secure storage for the key.
access_and_usage.subscription: No entitlement check found in the local-llm files read; Local is free where technically available (doc: docs/product/commercial.md Launch Posture).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Context window bounded to 4096 minimum and 8192 maximum for mobile (tier3.ts:60-70); RAM minimum for multimodal (MULTIMODAL_MIN_RAM_MB); device tier minimum RAM 3500 MB for the second tier (capabilities.ts:5). Local use is not metered by the code read.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Only models in the local catalog and fitting RAM and runtime; tools in Local mode are not used (doc: requirements.md:133).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: No provider for Local; mobile has no BYOK in v1 (doc: commercial.md).
access_and_usage.local_mode: This is the Local mode implementation on mobile: data and inference on the device with no account. Desktop Electron refuses local inference; CLI local routes exist but were not read.

corrections.claim: Schema migrations on open using PRAGMA user_version (db.ts:105-122)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The behaviour is right, but runMigrations is at db.ts:114-128, so the cited range misses part of it.

corrections.claim: Limits: context window bounded to 4096 minimum and 8192 maximum for mobile (tier3.ts:60-70); device tier minimum RAM 3500 MB for the second tier (capabilities.ts:5)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The values are right. tier3.ts:45-46 defines DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS = 4096 and MAX_MOBILE_CONTEXT_TOKENS = 8192. The clamp is at tier3.ts:70-75, and it falls back to 4096 when the catalog gives no context. capabilities.ts:4 defines the 3500 constant, used at line 76 (tier 2 is available when RAM is at least 3500, or RAM is unknown and the ExecuTorch runtime exists). The page cites the wrong lines.
corrections.correction: Context is clamped to 4096-8192, defaulting to 4096 (tier3.ts:45-46,70-75). Tier 2 needs 3500 MB of RAM, or unknown RAM with the ExecuTorch runtime present (capabilities.ts:4,75-77).

corrections.claim: Account: Not required for Local. Cloud route in onboarding needs sign-in.
corrections.what_the_code_shows: No Clerk sign-in is needed for Local (rootRouting.ts:44-57, onboarding.tsx:804-808 'Sign in to use Cloud'). But a first-launch age gate comes first. rootRouting.ts:38-43 sends anyone with ageGateConfirmed false to /age-gate before onboarding, and ageGate.ts applies region thresholds. So the person confirms their age before reaching Local chat. This matches the owner decision that every surface is 18 and over.
corrections.correction: No account is needed for Local, but the first-run age gate must be passed first. Cloud use needs sign-in.

corrections.claim: Subscription: no entitlement check found in the local-llm files read; Local is free where technically available
corrections.what_the_code_shows: docs/product/commercial.md:22 says Local is 'Free to use where technically available'. The grep for entitlement, plan and subscription in packages/platform/local-llm/src matched only catalog.ts, so the page's 'not found' is consistent with the code. I did not open that hit to see what it is. The page also flags this as unverified.
corrections.correction: Acceptable as worded. It is an absence-of-evidence statement, not a verified rule.

missing_facts: First-run age gate: rootRouting.ts:38-43 redirects any user without a confirmed age to /age-gate before onboarding. ageGate.ts:1-58 applies region thresholds (18 in India and Brazil timezones, otherwise ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE). The page's Journey, acceptance criteria and 'no account needed' text omit this. It is a mandatory step before Local chat.
Onboarding shows a first-run disclosure with consent acceptance before the 'about-you' screen (onboarding.tsx:280-305, using mmkvDisclosureLedger). The page does not mention it.

Electron's refusal is deliberate and cross-referenced: dispatcher.ts:3234-3244 says local coding sessions reach local models through the bundled CLI. The page says 'CLI local routes exist but were not read', so it misses a stated path for on-device inference on desktop.
